full_judgment:
11. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, learned advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners took the revisional application, the impugned judgment and decree, the pleadings of the respective parties, the deposition of all the P. W.s and D. W.s and the documents exhibited by the parties and submits that the plaintiffs have lawful right, title, interest and possession in the suit land on the strength of their predecessor's registered sale deed dated 15.06.1982 (Exhibit- 5) and the said registered sale deed being a document of title, will prevail over the so-called and non-existent S.A. khatian mysteriously prepared in the name of the Government. In this connection Mr. Bhuiyan placed reliance on 18 BLC (AD) 44; 13 MLR (AD) 6; 32 DLR 252; and 5 MLR 374. 

 12. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan further submits that the defendants miserably failed to prove that the suit land vested in the Government as khas land during the S. A. operation, in view of the fact that neither they adduced any minimum iota of evidence including the khas khatian itself before the courts below in support of their contention nor did they disclose the source through which or what basis or the manner in which the suit land devolved upon the Government and as such the plea of khas khatian which is the genesis of the defendants' case falls flat and therefore, the suit was rightly decreed by the trial Court. In this connection Mr. Bhuiyan drew the attention to Section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and referred to the decisions of Geeta Rani alais Shamima Khatun vs. Bangladesh, 36 DLR (AD) 225; Bangladesh and others vs. Mallick Ali Ahmed and others, 3CLR (AD) 345; and Md. Kalam Mollah and others vs. Sheikh Samsu and others, 23 BLT 320, which will be discussed later on. 

 14. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan next submits that none of the defendants specifically denied the accuracy or genuineness of R. S. Khatian No. 259 (Exhibit- 1/Ka) and they did not take any step against the said R. S. Khatian prepared and published in the name of Satish Chandra Das and as such the same has got presumptive value of correction in view of the case, of Government of Bangladesh and others vs. Mrs. Mohsina Rahaman alias Joya as reported in 50 DLR 186 wherein it has been held that: 

 17. Mr. Bhuiyan submits that the lower appellate court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure justice in failing to appreciate that the plaintiff-petitioners have been claiming title to 18.50 decimals of land in Plot No. 185 of R.S. Khatian No. 259 but not from R.S. Khatian No. 148 and an explanation has been offered in paragraph 3 of the plaint that  “প্রকাশ থাকে যে, বাদীর বায়ার আজাহার আলী মিয়া গংদের নিকট হইতে তাহাদের স্বত্তের কাগজপত্রের মধ্যে উক্ত খাজনার মোকদ্দমার কতক জাবেদা নকল সরবরাহ করেন ৷ উক্ত জাবেদা নকল পর্যালোচনার দেখা যায় ছোলে নামায় নালিশী আর, এস, ১৮৫ দাগটি আর.এস, ২৫৯ নং খতিয়ানের ভূমি। আর, এস, ২৫৯ নং এবং ১৪৮ নং খতিয়ানের প্রত্যেক খতিয়ানেই সতীশ চন্দ্র দাস স্বত্ববান থাকেন বিধায় বন্দোবস্ত প্রদান করেন এবং বাদীর নামীয় ইং ১৫-০৬-৮২ তারিখের 8২৩৯ নং দলিলের 

 18. On the above point Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that the explanation offered in the plaint has been substantiated by evidence, and that although R. S. Khatian No. 148 instead of Khatian No. 259 (lands of both the khatians belonged to Satish Chandra Das) has been inserted in the sale deed dated 15.06.1982, the same has in no way affected the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiff-petitioners in the suit land since they had been enjoying and possessing the same openly, adversely and peacefully to the knowledge of all concerned including the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 since their predecessor's sale deed dated 15.06.1982 and no one raised any objection claiming title to the suit land. 

 26. Mr. Shah Hossain next submits that the S. A. Khatian prepared and published in the name of the Government vis-a-vis the suit land shall be presumed to be correct unless and until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. In this connection Mr. Hossain referred to Section 19(3) and 144A of the SAT Act and the decisions reported in 9 MLR (AD) 82; 30 DLR (SC) 81; 6 BLC 241; 33 DLR 126; 17 BLC (AD) 174; and 61 DLR 18. 

 27. Mr. Shah Hossain finally submits that the trial Court wrongly shifted the burden of proving the correctness of S. A. Khatian on the defendant-opposite parties and held that the defendants failed to proves as to how, why and when the suit land became the khas land of the Government by adducing any evidence, oral and documentary. On this point Mr. Hossain further submits that as plaintiff-the petitioners ought to have proved their case, they cannot take the advantage of the weakness of the defendants. Supporting the impugned judgment and decree Mr. Hossain lastly submits that the appellate court below as the final court of fact arrived at a proper decision upon proper assessment of the pleadings of the parties, evidence and other materials on record and as such the same does not call for any interference from this Court. 

 28. I have meticulously gone through the revisional application, the impugned judgment and decree, the pleadings of the respective parties, evidence led by them and other materials on record and also heard the learned Advocates for both the sides at length and perused the decisions relied upon by both the parties with utmost circumspection and the relevant provisions of law wherefrom it transpires that the evidentiary value of the registered sale deed of the plaintiff-petitioners (Exhibit- 5), the preparation and publication of S. A. record of rights, if any, in the khas khatian of the Government as well as the maintainability of Rent Suit No. 60 of 1957 are predominant issues in this case apart from other connected issues and I will endeavour to address all the issues in proportion to their respective weight and importance. 

 29. It appears from the certified copy of the sale deed dated 15.06.1982 that the plaintiffs acquired title to the suit land on the strength of the same and the said registered sale deed being a document of title, will prevail over the so-called and non-existent S. A. khatian mysteriously prepared in the name of the Government as our Appellate Division has correctly held in the case of Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan and others vs. Md. Nasir Hossain and others, 18 BLC (AD) 44 in the following language: 

 30. It is the case of the defendant-opposite parties that the suit land vested in the Government as khas land during the S. A. operation, but none of them adduced any evidence including the khas khatian itself before the courts below in support of their contention. Again, although the Government filed a written statement, they did not adduce any evidence, oral or documentary, to show as to when, why and how the suit land became khas in their name and as such the written statement of the Government will not ipso facto be admissible in evidence unless and until the same is supported by competent witnesses of convincing nature, and as such Section 92 of the SAT Act as well as the decisions referred to by the plaintiff-petitioner will stand in the way of the claim of defendants. At this juncture I think it is necessary to quote Section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, which runs as follows: 

 35. In the panorama as canvassed in the foregoing paragraph, it can be safely concluded that the defendants are not absolved of their obligation to prove as to when, why and how the suit land was recorded in the khas khatian of the Government and that obligation having not been discharged by any of the defendants, the plea of khas khatian is not proved at all. Moreover, it has already been held in Civil Revision No. 2613 of 2011 arising out of Title Suit No. 55 of 200 to which the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are plaintiffs that the opposite parties of the present Rule signally failed to prove their plea as to khas khatian. 

 36. It appears from R. S. Khatian No. 259 (Ext. 1/Ka) that R. S. Plot No. 185 is present in the said khatian showing 37 decimals of land in sixteen annas share and on scrutiny of R. S. Khatian No. 148, it is found that Plot No. 285 appears therein, but the quantum of land in the said plot is completely different, namely 15 decimals in eight annas share, and thus, I am of the view that the explanation offered in the plaint as to the insertion of R. S. Khatian No. 148 in lieu of R. S. Khatian it No. 259 in the compromise decree dated 26.02.1957 as drawn up in Rent Suit No. 60 of 1957 and the subsequent sale deeds appears to be plausible and acceptable. 

 opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 entered into the suit land after the flood of 1988, whereas they allegedly took settlement of the same in 1999 and they did not at all clarify in their pleadings submitted and evidence adduced in all the suits in what capacity they possessed and enjoyed the suit land for the intervening period between 1988 and 1999 and as such I am constrained to hold the view that the plaintiffs entered into the suit land as mere trespassers. Moreover, Court think that if the suit land had ever been recorded in the khas khatian of the Government, it would have settled the same in favour of anyone else, and in the absence of any such lease, Government's title as well as the interest of the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 in the suit land is not proved at all.
